name: Coral bleaching
summary: No global bleaching event since June; El Niño raises risk this southern summer
state: NOAA confirmed in June 2026 that the fourth global coral bleaching event had ended. Reef agencies in the Seychelles and Caribbean have warned that the strong El Niño could trigger new bleaching as Southern Hemisphere waters warm; no new regional mass bleaching was confirmed as of 2 Nov.
for_you: Reef-dependent fisheries and tourism face renewed risk over the coming southern summer.
rubric_hit: No global bleaching event in progress

sources.title: GCRMN — Fourth global bleaching event ended
Nature Seychelles — What a strong El Niño warning means for coral reefs

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.
rubric.watch: Global bleaching event in progress, or regional mass bleaching.
rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.
